panels.title: The two new trackers’ step names
panels.lede: Rules 11.10 and 11.11 track a state ballot measure and a federal court case in six steps each, on the bill tracker’s marks. Their twelve step names come from the law, each with its source, and they wait for your word as the bill’s six did (DR-108).

items.title: Rule 11.10, a state ballot measure, in six steps
items.answer: The six names are Filed, Title and summary, Signatures, Legislature, On the ballot and Vote. Step 4 holds only where a state’s initiative goes to the Legislature first; a measure that goes straight to the ballot keeps step 4 under a slash, as the bill tracker marks a step that never happened.
items.what_changed: New in round 5 (C-118). The plate draws three invented measures, each labeled Illustrative: one counted but not yet certified, one approved by voters and certified, and one that failed to qualify, which ends on a square at step 3. A table after the rule gives each step, what happens at it and where the law of Massachusetts, California, Ohio and Michigan sets it. The review’s fixes changed words only (C-123), and the second pass gave the plate’s alt its title and key, so a screen reader hears it once (RS-1).
items.why: DR-108 approved the bill’s six names by name, and DR-231 puts these trackers under the same rule, so their names need the same word from you.
items.recommendation: Approve the six names as the plate prints them.

steps.name: Filed
steps.what_happens: The sponsors file the measure’s full text with the attorney general.
steps.law: Massachusetts Constitution, Amendment Article XLVIII, The Initiative, II, Section 3, as replaced by Amendment Article LXXIV, Section 1; California Elections Code 9001

steps.name: Title and summary
steps.what_happens: The attorney general writes the title and summary that petitions and ballots carry, and where the law asks, first certifies that the measure is in proper form and on a subject the initiative may cover.
steps.law: Massachusetts, Amendment Article LXXIV, Sections 1 and 4; California Elections Code 9004 and 9014

steps.name: Signatures
steps.what_happens: The sponsors gather signatures, and election officials count and check them.
steps.law: Massachusetts, Amendment Article LXXIV, Section 1; California Elections Code 9030 and 9031

steps.name: Legislature
steps.what_happens: The Legislature votes on the measure first, where the state’s initiative is indirect. A measure that goes straight to the ballot keeps this step under a slash.
steps.law: Massachusetts, Amendment Article LXXXI, Section 2; Ohio Constitution, Article II, Section 1b; Michigan Constitution, Article II, Section 9

steps.name: On the ballot
steps.what_happens: The state’s election officer certifies the measure for the ballot.
steps.law: California Elections Code 9033; Massachusetts, Amendment Article LXXXI, Section 2

steps.name: Vote
steps.what_happens: The voters decide, and the state certifies the result.
steps.law: California Constitution, Article II, Section 10(a); Massachusetts, Amendment Article LXXXI, Section 2; Ohio, Article II, Section 1b; Michigan, Article II, Section 9

items.title: Rule 11.11, a federal court case, in six steps
items.answer: The six names are Filed, Trial court ruling, Appeal, Appeals court ruling, Supreme Court petition and Supreme Court ruling. A petition the Supreme Court denies ends on a square at step 5, and the appeals court’s ruling stands.
items.what_changed: New in round 5 (C-118). The plate draws three invented federal civil cases, each labeled Illustrative: one argued and waiting on the appeals court, one reversed and sent back by the Supreme Court, and one whose petition the Court denied. A table after the rule gives each step and the rule or statute behind it. The review’s fixes changed words only, among them a ruling no one appeals, which keeps the steps after it under slashes (C-123, calls 4 and 5); the second pass gave the plate’s alt its title and key (RS-1).
items.why: As for Rule 11.10: DR-231 puts the court case tracker under DR-108, which approved the bill’s names by name.
items.recommendation: Approve the six names as the plate prints them.

steps.name: Filed
steps.what_happens: One side sues the other in a federal district court, the trial court.
steps.law: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 3; 28 U.S.C. 1331

steps.name: Trial court ruling
steps.what_happens: The trial court decides, with or without a trial, unless the case settles or is dismissed.
steps.law: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 41, 56 and 58

steps.name: Appeal
steps.what_happens: The side that lost asks a court of appeals to review the ruling.
steps.law: 28 U.S.C. 1291 and 2107; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rule 4

steps.name: Appeals court ruling
steps.what_happens: Three judges of the court of appeals decide.
steps.law: 28 U.S.C. 2106; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure, Rules 40 and 41

steps.name: Supreme Court petition
steps.what_happens: The side that lost asks the Supreme Court to hear the case, and the Court agrees or declines.
steps.law: Rules of the Supreme Court, Rules 10, 13 and 16; 28 U.S.C. 1254 and 2101

steps.name: Supreme Court ruling
steps.law: 28 U.S.C. 2106; Rules of the Supreme Court, Rule 16

facts.label: The docket’s word
facts.value: “Affirmed”, explained once in the rule’s text (ED5-3)

rows.code: CR-S4, Rule 15.19's order and a sticky drawing
rows.where: Rule 15.19, `s-15-19-correct`, `rule_15_19()` in `work/build/scripts/phase-3/phase3_ch15_build.py` (near line 3195); the shell's plate frame, `.plate-scroll` in `work/build/guide/shell/guide-shell.css`
rows.what_is_wrong: Rules 15.19 and 14.143 set the same stepper's parts in two orders; at a desk 15.19's drawing ends about 340 px above Play, so its column stands empty while a reader steps through the list
rows.suggested_fix: Order: in `rule_15_19()`, `right` becomes the status line, the controls, the reason line, then the step list and the limit's note, as on 14.143, so Tab reaches Play, Reset the loop, Previous step and Next step before the list; the shared script reads parts by class and needs no change. rows.why_not_made: The order waits on the accessibility lead's yes to the new focus order (CR-S4's condition), and the systems designer's notes record no change; every plate frame scrolls sideways today (`overflow-x: auto`), so a sticky part sticks to its frame, and changing that reaches every frame's clipping and keyboard scrolling
rows.status: Open (the order); the sticky drawing, and a sticky control row on a phone, held for Dustin (board 3)
